body:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) is investing as much as $57.5 million in an Asia green infrastructure credit fund under BlackRock.

It has committed up to $30 million to the Emerging Asia Infrastructure Credit Fund (EAIC), which is managed by BlackRock’s Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) and is part of Singapore’s blended finance programme FAST-P.

Alongside its own commitment, ADB will administer investments of up to $10 million from the Canadian Climate and Nature Fund for the Private Sector in Asia (CANPA) and up to $17.5 million from the Australian Climate Finance Partnership (ACFP).

CANPA is a trust fund managed by ADB and supported by a commitment of C$360 million from the Government of Canada.

ACFP, managed by the ADB and funded by an Australian Government contribution of up to A$140 million, aims to unlock private investment for initiatives related to the changing climate across Southeast Asia and the Pacific.

ADB added that the Japan International Cooperation Agency is also investing in EAIC.

The infrastructure lending fund, with a targeted $750-million size, will focus on Southeast Asia, investing across the themes of transition to a low-carbon economy, transition of hard-to-abate sectors, as well as emerging decarbonisation technologies. It will build a portfolio of 10–20 investments, primarily through senior and mezzanine debt instruments.

“Mobilising private capital at scale is essential to addressing Asia’s development and sustainability challenges. Through this Monetary Authority of Singapore-led initiative, ADB aims to catalyse innovative financing solutions, strengthen investment structures and demonstrate viable pathways for private sector participation,” said Isabel Chatterton, ADB Director General, Private Sector Operations Department.

ADB’s participation aims to help expand financing for sustainable infrastructure projects and companies, particularly in sectors where access to long-term capital remains constrained. The FAST-P structure brings together catalytic and commercial capital to mitigate investment risks and attract institutional investors to opportunities in developing markets.
